column1: # Which Conventional Commits type a measured change shape falls under, and which shapes fall
# under none. The type and definition columns are quoted from conventional-commit-types.tsv,
# which carries the publishers' own words; the shape and measurement columns are this
# library's, and the pairing is checkable by reading one against the other — a change that
# only adds declarations against "a commit of the type feat introduces a new feature".
# The rules are ordered and the first whose shape a change has answers, so a change confined
# to the source sets that check the published ones is a test even where it adds declarations:
# nothing the build publishes moved. A shape with an empty type states an abstention, and the
# note says what stops the reading naming it.
# Columns: shape, measurement, type, definition, note.
#   shape        the token the reading names this shape by
#   measurement  what is measured to decide it, as a clause completing "it ..."
#   type         the Conventional Commits token, or empty where no definition covers the shape
#   definition   the publisher's own sentence for that token, quoted
#   note         why the reading names nothing, on the rows where it does not
# Name: Conventional Commits types by measured change shape
# Publisher: this library, quoting the Conventional Commits contributors
#   (https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) and the Angular convention
# Kind: mappings
# Source: the definitions are quoted from conventional-commit-types.tsv, which extracts them
#   from the specification at v1.0.0 and from @commitlint/config-conventional at the revision
#   the specification's own link pins. The shapes and the pairings are this library's.
# Licence: the Conventional Commits specification is CC BY 3.0. The pairings carry the
#   licence of this library.
documentation-only
checks-only
column2: changes only the files that check what the build publishes
column4: Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests

column1: build-only
column4: Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies (example scopes: gulp, broccoli, npm)

column1: adds-declarations
column4: a commit of the type feat introduces a new feature to the codebase (this correlates with MINOR in Semantic Versioning).

column1: removes-declarations
column5: Semantic Versioning calls removing something from the published API an incompatible change, which the specification correlates with the BREAKING CHANGE footer. The parse states which declaration a name is and who chose it, never whether the published surface carries it, so the reading cannot tell a removal from the published API from a removal of something private, and names nothing.

column1: adds-and-removes-declarations
column5: More than one definition covers it — a commit can add a feature and repair a defect in one change — and nothing measured here chooses between them.

column1: changes-bodies
column2: changes lines and neither adds nor removes a declaration
column5: The Angular convention defines refactor as a change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature, and the specification defines fix as one that repairs a defect. Both cover a change confined to method bodies, and nothing measured here separates them.
